name: Accra
tagline: West Africa's Friendliest City with Beaches, Culture, and Growing Modernity
description: Accra is one of Africa's most welcoming cities for expats, with English as the official language, a stable democracy, and a warm, open culture that makes newcomers feel at home quickly. The city offers Atlantic Ocean beaches, a vibrant nightlife and music scene rooted in highlife and afrobeats, and a rapidly modernizing infrastructure. For FIRE retirees, Accra delivers strong value with affordable housing, excellent tropical fruit and seafood, and a growing community of international residents. Ghana's Year of Return initiative has made the country especially popular with African American retirees.

quickFacts.visa: Visa required for US citizens (available on arrival or online, 60 days). Right to Abode permit for long-term stays. No dedicated retirement visa — residence permits available through investment or extended stay applications.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Good – one of the safest countries in West Africa
quickFacts.climate: Tropical savanna with hot temperatures year-round and a rainy season

housing.description: Secure gated 1BR/studio (24/7 guard, generator, water tank) on the East Legon fringe, Osu, or Labone — the security premium a solo expat actually pays

dining.description: Chop-bar and local eats a few times a week; mostly home cooking

healthcare.description: Basic local/regional private cover, single adult 45–55, hospitalization-first

transportation.description: Bolt/Uber daily plus the occasional trotro; no car

1M.lifestyle: A small but secure gated 1BR or studio on the East Legon fringe, Osu, or Labone — the 24/7 guard, generator, and water tank are the security premium a solo retiree actually pays for here. Most meals are cooked at home from local markets, with chop-bar plates a few times a week, and you get around by Bolt and the occasional trotro rather than owning a car. Cover is a no-frills local/regional plan handling hospitalization and basic outpatient care. AC use is rationed against the prepaid meter, and dumsor means the inverter earns its keep. Comfortable and safe, but genuinely frugal — no imported-grocery habit and little travel.

housing.description: Nicer furnished 1BR in Osu, Labone, or Cantonments

dining.description: Out several nights a week, local + mid-range

healthcare.description: Comprehensive regional private cover (Nyaho, Akai House access)

entertainment.description: Gym plus a regular social life

2M.lifestyle: A nicer furnished 1BR in Osu, Labone, or Cantonments, within walking distance of restaurants and nightlife. Groceries mix Makola-market local produce with imported items, and dinners out several nights a week are routine. Comprehensive regional private insurance covers the good private clinics like Nyaho and Akai House. Daily Bolt rides replace the trotro entirely, and a gym membership plus an active weekend social life round out an easy, unpretentious solo life.

3M.lifestyle: A good furnished/serviced 1BR in a prime pocket like Cantonments or Airport Residential — 24-hour security, backup power, and a gym come built in, which matters when dumsor hits. Dining at Accra's better restaurants becomes a default, and transport is either an owned car or unlimited Bolt with an occasional hired day-driver. Insurance steps up to a strong plan approaching international cover, with regional referral. Weekends mean Cape Coast, Ada, or the Aburi hills, with real budget margin left over each month.

5M.lifestyle: A top luxury serviced 1BR or small 2BR kept for one in Cantonments or Airport Residential, with a part-time housekeeper/cook and a part-time driver handling an owned car. Dining is near-daily at Accra's top spots, backed by a club or beach-club membership and frequent regional travel. Healthcare is a top-tier international plan (worldwide-excl-US) with evacuation cover to South Africa or Europe. A full-AC flat or villa with its own generator means dumsor is somebody else's problem, and there is generous discretionary room for one person.

10M.lifestyle: The top of what one person can consume in Accra — a solo-luxury 1–2BR or small villa at the best address in Cantonments or Airport Residential, staffed by a full-time housekeeper, cook, and driver scaled to a single home rather than an estate's crew. Daily fine dining and hosting, first-class regional and international travel, and an international concierge health plan with worldwide access and evacuation. A large villa runs on its own generator against dumsor, and the discretionary budget funds concierge services, club tiers, and hobbies. It sits well below a family FatFIRE precisely because a solo resident can't fill a household's bedrooms, food, or fleet.
